title_original: Bruce Greenwood, Johnny Knoxville And Dylan Hawco Join ‘Fake Skating’ Adaptation At Sony
excerpt_original: EXCLUSIVE: Bruce Greenwood, Johnny Knoxville and Dylan Hawco are set to round out the cast in Sony Pictures and Will Gluck’s Olive Bridge Entertainment’s Fake Skating based on Lynn Painter’s New York Times best-selling book with Amélie Hoeferle and Graham Campbell set to star.…

blocks.text: EXCLUSIVE: Bruce Greenwood , Johnny Knoxville and Dylan Hawco are set to round out the cast in Sony Pictures and Will Gluck’s Olive Bridge Entertainment’s Fake Skating based on Lynn Painter’s New York Times best-selling book with Amélie Hoeferle and Graham Campbell set to star. Josh Boone is directing from a screenplay written by Morgan Lehmann and Victoria Bata with revisions by Boone and his writing partner Knate Lee.

This is the first book from the best-selling author to be adapted for the screen. Set for a summer release next year, Fake Skating is an emotional high school hockey romance about childhood sweethearts whose icy reunion in their hockey-loving hometown unexpectedly thaws when they fake a romantic relationship.

blocks.text: Winner of the 2025 Goodreads Choice Award for Young Adult Fiction, Fake Skating has nearly 500,000 copies in print and has appeared on the New York Times YA Hardcover Bestseller list 48 times since its release in September 2025, holding the #1 spot for 15 of those weeks. The novel has also been translated into 16 languages.

Painter is the #1 New York Times and internationally best-selling author of Better Than the Movies, The Do-Over, Betting on You, Maid For Each Other, First and Forever, Nothing Like the Movies, and Fake Skating .

Greenwood is best known for his roles in the film Thirteen Days where he portrayed President John F. Kennedy. Other notable film credits include I, Robot , Double Jeopardy , Capote , Star Trek and Star Trek Into Darkness, and The Post . His television credits include The Resident and the miniseries The Fall of the House of Usher. He is repped by Gersh and Binder & Associates.
Knoxville can recently be seen in I Want Your Sex, Tiny Fugitives, and as the host of Fear Factor: House of Fear . He is repped by CAA and Sloane Offer.

Hawco will next be seen starring in Sarah Polley’s film adaptation of The Bell Jar. His recent credits include Youngblood and Eli Roth’s horror film Ice Cream Man. He is repped by GGA, Gersh, and Circle Management + Production.
